shell-escape.comment: 028-identifier-highlighting: a ShellEscape statement (statement.rs's classify_statement: first token is a bare '*' punctuation) is one physical line of literal OS shell text, not Voyager syntax at all -- one flat match over the whole line (leading '*' included) so nothing else, old pattern or new, ever matches inside it (research.md Sec 5). Matches only when '*' is the first non-whitespace character on its physical line, the same statement-start shape voyager-core's own parser requires; a bare '*' used as multiplication mid-expression is never at line-start, so this never misfires there.
shell-escape.name: meta.embedded.shell-escape.drut

label.comment: 028-identifier-highlighting: a Label statement (statement.rs: first token ':' punctuation, second is the name) is exactly this shape -- one flat match, own scope, so the name is claimed here rather than by #user-identifiers (research.md Sec 5). Bonus: labels get real, dedicated highlighting for the first time (previously unstyled).
label.name: entity.name.label.drut

string-escape.comment: Backslash escapes inside a quoted string (e.g. the \n seen throughout the real corpus's PRINT LIST='...\n' values) -- constant.character.escape, the same scope Python/JS/shell grammars all use for this, so it reads distinctly from the surrounding string text under any theme.
string-escape.name: constant.character.escape.drut

variable-ref.comment: @name@ substitution. One uniform scope over the whole match (delimiters included), not split into begin/name/end captures -- a prior version scoped the @ delimiters as punctuation.definition.variable.* separately from the name's variable.other.readwrite, which most themes render in a different (often muted) color from the name, since punctuation.definition.* is a distinct, more-specific selector many themes have their own rule for (issue #2: users want the entire @token@, @ included, to read as one color, distinct from string). variable.other.readwrite is kept as the scope (rather than e.g. bhereth's entity.name.tag) since it's already validated against real theme testing (2026-08-10: a bare custom variable.other.substitution.<lang> leaf scope rendered with no color at all under a stock dark theme; variable.other.readwrite -- the same convention shell-script grammars use for $VAR -- did not have that problem).
variable-ref.name: variable.other.readwrite.drut

statement-words.comment: General (non-block-structural) statement/procedure words -- deliberately a *different* scope (support.function, the conventional TextMate category for a language's built-in commands/procedures, as distinct from true control-flow keywords) so they read visually distinct from control-words above, the same two-tier convention most language grammars use for control-flow vs. builtin-function keywords. Real-usage-evidenced (constitution Principle II: never vendor-doc-copied) -- corpus census against the full 161-file WF-TDM-Official-Releases corpus, 2026-08-10, same distinct_files>=3 threshold 001-voyager-script-parser/003-lsp-vscode-extension's own censuses already established, words already covered by control-words above excluded. Not exhaustive by construction (any word not in this list still parses and functions identically -- FR-003 establishes there's no closed vocabulary -- it just renders unstyled, the same as before this list existed). 026-highlight-customization: scope renamed from the shared support.function.drut to support.function.statement.drut (a pure rename, no match-pattern change) so this category and #function-calls below are independently colorable via drut.highlight.statementWords/drut.highlight.functionCalls -- any theme with no rule for either specific name still falls back to its own support.function-prefix rule, so this is not a visible behavior change on its own.
statement-words.name: support.function.statement.drut

function-calls.comment: 024-function-call-highlighting: a Cube Voyager built-in function name, matched only when immediately followed by '(' with zero intervening whitespace -- the unambiguous call position, since Voyager has no user-definable functions (a coincidentally-named array/matrix element access, e.g. a user array literally called MAX indexed as MAX(1), is an accepted rare false positive; see spec.md Edge Cases). Deliberately a *separate* pattern from #statement-words (which matches unconditionally, with no '('-lookahead) rather than an addition to it, so a bareword that merely spells a recognized function name -- e.g. a keyword=value pair literally named MAX -- is never miscolored when no call is present. This list is comprehensive by direct reading of every function-related chapter in two local vendor documentation mirrors (Cube Voyager 6.5.1 and OpenPaths Cube/CUBE CONNECT Edition; never committed, gitignored, research-only per CLAUDE.md) plus one real-corpus-confirmed addition absent from both editions (PRINTPROGRESS) -- see specs/024-function-call-highlighting/research.md for the full 138-name source list, category breakdown, and cross-version validation. Deliberately excludes a separate camelCase object-model/scripting-API surface found in the same OpenPaths docs (e.g. addNonTransitLeg()) -- out of scope for the Voyager control-statement language this grammar targets. Also deliberately excludes three real, vendor-documented Public Transport skim values (BESTJRNY, EXCESSDEMAND, EXCESSPROP) that are conventionally used without a trailing '(...)' at all, since this pattern's entire mechanism keys off the '(' lookahead. Not exhaustive by construction (research.md Sec 5): a genuine built-in function not yet in this list renders unstyled, exactly as before this pattern existed, the same non-exhaustive stance #statement-words already documents for itself. 026-highlight-customization: scope renamed from the shared support.function.drut to support.function.builtin.drut (a pure rename, no match-pattern change) -- see #statement-words' own comment above for why.
function-calls.name: support.function.builtin.drut

data-references.comment: 028-identifier-highlighting: the Matrix/Line/Node/Zone/Database data-reference family voyager-core's data_reference.rs already recognizes for casing (MI/MO/MW/LI/LW/NI/NW/ZI/ZONES/Z/DBI/DBA/RO/A/B/I/J) -- matched case-insensitively by exact name or dot-notation prefix (dba.2.field), regardless of position (research.md Sec 2). The trailing lookahead (a literal '.' for dot-notation, or a non-identifier boundary for a bare occurrence) means alternative order inside the group doesn't matter for correctness even though some names are string-prefixes of others (Z of ZI/ZONES) -- a premature Z-only match against ZONES fails its own lookahead (next char is a word char) and falls through to the ZONES alternative. Listed before #pair-keywords/#pair-values so a name that's also keyword-pair-shaped (e.g. ZONES in RUN PGM=MATRIX ZONES=5) is claimed here instead -- one name, one owning category, mirroring data_reference.rs's own FR-005 rule (research.md Sec 3).
data-references.name: variable.language.data-reference.drut

pair-keywords.comment: A keyword=value pair's keyword name (optionally bracket-subscripted, e.g. VOL[01]=), colored like a Python keyword argument's parameter name (func(param=value)) -- variable.parameter, distinct from control-words/statement-words above. Deliberately structural/generic (matches FR-003's `word[subscript]=` shape from voyager-core's own grammar, not a fixed name list) rather than vendor-sourced, since FR-003 already establishes there's no closed keyword vocabulary. Listed after control-words/statement-words in the top-level patterns array so a word like PHASE (control-words) or PRINT (statement-words) that's *also* immediately followed by = still gets its more specific scope -- TextMate resolves same-position ties by array order.

pair-values.comment: A bareword value immediately after = (or <=/>=/<>/==, since the lookbehind only checks for a literal = as the last character of whatever operator preceded it) -- e.g. MATRIX/HWYASSIGN in PGM=MATRIX/PGM=HWYASSIGN, real Cube Voyager program names with no closed enumeration this grammar hand-lists (same FR-003 no-closed-vocabulary stance as #pair-keywords/#statement-words) -- colored generically as constant.other, the same convention many grammars use for an enum-like bareword value distinct from a quoted string or a number. Deliberately does not fire inside a quoted string (this pattern is top-level-only; #strings' own begin/end block has its own separate, short patterns list -- variable-ref and string-escape only -- so string *content* is never reachable from here). The trailing negative lookahead excludes a bareword that's actually the first operand of a larger expression (LINKID = _ANode + '_' + _BNode's _ANode) -- a genuine keyword=value pair is never itself followed by an operator, quote, paren, or bracket, so this narrows the position-based heuristic without needing a real parse tree; a bareword that IS the entire assignment RHS (X = _ANode alone) still can't be told apart from a real pair value and keeps this scope (028-identifier-highlighting follow-up).
pair-values.name: constant.other.drut

numbers.comment: A numeric literal, negative sign included only when it can't plausibly be a binary minus (guarded by the same not-preceded-by-alnum-or-closing-bracket lookbehind an operator-precedence-aware tokenizer would use) -- e.g. ZONES=-5's -5 is one number, but 2-2's - is left for #operators to claim as subtraction.
numbers.name: constant.numeric.drut

operators.comment: Symbol-only, structural -- no word-shaped logical operators (AND/OR/NOT-style) included, since those would need the same real-corpus evidence standard this grammar already holds keyword lists to, and none has been gathered for them.
operators.name: keyword.operator.drut

user-identifiers.comment: 028-identifier-highlighting: catch-all for a bareword identifier not already claimed by an earlier, more specific pattern (control word, statement word, function-call name, #data-references, pair-keyword name, pair value) -- placed last in the top-level patterns array, so array position alone is the entire filtering mechanism (research.md Sec 4). This is what makes FR-004's 'none of the above' definition free: it falls out of pattern-list order, not a hand-written negative-lookahead blacklist that would have to duplicate every other pattern's word list inline. A bareword immediately adjacent to '=' is never offered to this pattern at all -- #pair-keywords/#pair-values are listed well before this one and already claim that shape (spec.md Assumptions' documented =-adjacency trade-off).
user-identifiers.name: variable.other.identifier.drut
